news.title: U.S. Shale Giants Hold Back on Drilling Despite Higher Oil Prices
news.summary: The biggest U.S. shale producers have remained conservative in spending on drilling this year despite the spike in the average WTI crude price by $20 per barrel compared to last year. While signs have emerged that smaller independents have started to take advantage of the higher oil prices to increase drilling, the biggest shale producers are keeping their powder dry amid unprecedented uncertainty in global markets. One of the top shale producers and the biggest Permian-only focused driller, Diamondback Energy, signaled this week that it will not…

analysis.summary: Major U.S. shale producers maintain capital discipline and hold back on drilling expansion despite higher crude prices.
analysis.rationale: Restrained drilling and capex discipline by large shale drillers limits new crude supply growth, exerting upward pressure on oil prices.

news.title: ConocoPhillips Doubles Profit to $4 Billion, Raises Dividend
news.summary: ConocoPhillips more than doubled its third-quarter profit to $4 billion and raised its quarterly dividend by 11% on Thursday, joining a growing list of oil majors reporting enormous earnings gains as higher crude prices offset production disruptions caused by the Iran war. The Houston-based producer reported adjusted earnings of $3.27 per share, comfortably beating Wall Street's $2.97 estimate. Net income jumped from $1.7 billion a year earlier, despite a decline in production. The company's average realized price climbed 32% year over year to…

analysis.summary: ConocoPhillips beat Wall Street expectations, doubling third-quarter profit to $4 billion and raising its dividend.
analysis.rationale: Strong quarterly corporate earnings reflect backward-looking realized crude prices and do not introduce a clear directional driver for future oil prices.
